title: Etsy Travel Pouch Order - Shipping Address Verification and Customer Reply
breadth_reason: This script tests Anticipy's ability to handle uploaded audio ASR for a specific e-commerce action on a signed-in Etsy order page, extending breadth by combining audio input with real surface verification and decision-making.

v7_target.surface_rule: user's signed-in Chrome profile with Etsy order page
v7_target.proof_rule: fresh surface-readable proof from public build

primary_user_input.reason: Uploaded audio ASR coverage ensures the system can process pre-recorded spoken instructions, expanding input modality beyond live mic or text paste.

real_user_surfaces.name: Etsy Order Page
real_user_surfaces.proof_needed: visible order details for the travel pouch

real_user_surfaces.name: Chrome Signed-In Profile
real_user_surfaces.surface: Chrome browser with user's Google account

moments.spoken_reference_text: On the Etsy order page for the travel pouch I bought for the Lisbon trip next month, please verify the shipping address and draft a customer reply to the seller about late delivery. If you cannot prove the visible Etsy order surface or my signed-in account, decline without changing anything.
moments.delivery_instruction: Per-run audio artifact must be generated via the 'say' command to ensure fresh ASR processing.

success_criteria: The uploaded audio is successfully transcribed and the ASR output matches the spoken reference text.
Anticipy verifies the user's signed-in Etsy order page surface using the real Chrome profile.
Anticipy either drafts a customer reply to the seller about late delivery and displays the shipping address, or declines if the surface is not verifiable.
The decision is based on fresh surface proof, not stale or cloned data.
The entire flow completes within the public product path from anticipy.ai/app to installed user-device engine.
failure_triggers: If the uploaded audio cannot be transcribed due to poor quality, format issues, or ASR failure.
If the Etsy order page is not visible or the user is not signed in to Chrome.
If the proof of surface is not fresh or originates from a cloned Chrome profile.
If the system attempts to act or ask without first verifying the real surface.
If the ASR output does not contain the expected intent or references the wrong order.
